slides.h: Hardware is the //jewellery// of a room.
slides.dek: The forty-gram detail the eye checks first.

slides.h: Builder-grade handles date a room instantly.
body: Hollow, shiny, and identical in every flat on the street.
The eye knows the weight of a handle before the hand ever reaches it.
Unlacquered brass, aged bronze, matte black. A finish that marks and mellows reads as material.
A mirror shine reads as coating, and coatings read as cost saved.

slides.h: Twelve pulls cost less than one chair.
body: Swapping every handle in the kitchen is one afternoon and a small spend.
It retunes the largest piece of furniture the room has.
Pick a family and let it repeat: handles, hinges, the tap, the picture light.
Repetition is what makes a detail read chosen instead of leftover.

slides.h: Save this before the next hardware aisle.
